primary_slope_adjusted.formula: realized_cer + n_errors + char_len + corrupted_negation + corrupted_numeral + C(family)
primary_slope_adjusted.engine: clustered_logit_fallback (idrift.analysis.mixed_models._fit_clustered_fallback, the same call idrift.analysis.run_v3 uses to produce stats_v3_digest.json's mixed_model.drift.coefficients.realized_cer)

slope_no_mediators.note: corrupted_negation and corrupted_numeral are downstream consequences of realized_cer (a negation/numeral token can only be corrupted if the corruption process, whose intensity IS realized_cer, happens to hit one), not confounders of it, so the ADJUSTED 5.41 estimates the DIRECT effect of realized_cer net of those two mediated pathways, while this no-mediators refit estimates the TOTAL effect of realized_cer on drift, including any part routed through flipping a negation or numeral.

per_model_slopes.method: message-clustered cluster-robust logit (drift ~ realized_cer), univariate, fit SEPARATELY within each model (idrift.analysis.dependence_sensitivity.per_model_pooled_slope's per-model fits) -- reported directly as the primary model-level summary, replacing the DerSimonian-Laird pooled figure

dl_pooled_descriptive_only.note: kept only as a SUPPLEMENTARY descriptive number, not the primary model-level estimator: the DerSimonian-Laird pool and its I^2 heterogeneity decomposition assume the 7 models are exchangeable draws from a population of studies, but these 7 are a convenience sample of whichever open-weight checkpoints fit the compute budget, not an inferential population of 'LLMs in general.' The per-model slopes and their descriptive min-max range above are the primary model-level summary.

vif.note: VIF for the 3 predictors the reviewer flagged as algebraically related (realized_cer is approximately n_errors / char_len by construction of the corruption process). Rule of thumb: VIF > 5 warrants attention, VIF > 10 indicates severe collinearity; none here reaches 10, so the adjusted model's realized_cer coefficient is estimable, though n_errors and realized_cer share meaningful variance as expected.

family_checkpoint_confound_note: family (the C(family) fixed effect in the adjusted model) is derived from model_id by stripping the size/tag suffix. Of the 4 families in this study's 7-checkpoint matrix, mistral-small and qwen3.5 each contribute exactly ONE checkpoint (mistral-small:24b; qwen3.5:27b-q4), so for those two families the family fixed effect is perfectly confounded with the checkpoint/model effect -- it cannot be attributed to 'being a Mistral-Small model' versus 'being specifically this 24b checkpoint.' Only gemma4 (3 checkpoints: 12b/31b/e4b) and phi4 (2 checkpoints: 14b/mini) let the design distinguish a within-family size/checkpoint effect from a between-family effect at all.
notes: Task A5 (reviewer #5): (a) per-model slopes + descriptive min-max range replace the DerSimonian-Laird pool as the primary model-level summary (7 convenience-selected checkpoints is not an inferential population for random-effects pooling); (b) VIF for realized_cer/n_errors/char_len answers the collinearity objection; (c) a no-mediators refit (dropping corrupted_negation/corrupted_numeral) reports the TOTAL corruption effect alongside the adjusted (direct) effect. primary_slope_adjusted reproduces output/stats_v3_digest.json's mixed_model.drift.coefficients.realized_cer (5.41 headline).
